From 1e446fd0582ad8be9f6dafb115fc2e7245f9bea7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 17:30:20 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] can: ucan: Fix infinite loop from zero-length messages

If a broken ucan device gets a message with the message length field set
to 0, then the driver will loop for forever in
ucan_read_bulk_callback(), hanging the system.  If the length is 0, just
skip the message and go on to the next one.

This has been fixed in the kvaser_usb driver in the past in commit
0c73772cd2b8 ("can: kvaser_usb: leaf: Fix potential infinite loop in
command parsers"), so there must be some broken devices out there like
this somewhere.

Cc: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>
Cc: Vincent Mailhol <mailhol@kernel.org>
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Assisted-by: gkh_clanker_2000
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/2026022319-huff-absurd-6a18@gregkh
Fixes: 9f2d3eae88d2 ("can: ucan: add driver for Theobroma Systems UCAN devices")
Signed-off-by: Marc Kleine-Budde <mkl@pengutronix.de>

diff --git a/drivers/net/can/usb/ucan.c b/drivers/net/can/usb/ucan.c
index c79508b1c43e..0ea0ac75e42f 100644
--- a/drivers/net/can/usb/ucan.c
+++ b/drivers/net/can/usb/ucan.c
@@ -748,7 +748,7 @@ static void ucan_read_bulk_callback(struct urb *urb)
 		len = le16_to_cpu(m->len);
 
 		/* check sanity (length of content) */
-		if (urb->actual_length - pos < len) {
+		if ((len == 0) || (urb->actual_length - pos < len)) {
 			netdev_warn(up->netdev,
 				    "invalid message (short; no data; l:%d)\n",
 				    urb->actual_length);
-- 
2.34.1

### Modifications in each file

- **`drivers/net/can/usb/ucan.c`**: In the function `ucan_read_bulk_callback()`, the sanity check for the message length was extended. Previously, the loop would only break if `urb->actual_length - pos < len` (i.e., the remaining buffer was too short). This check did not handle the case where the message length field `len` is zero. A zero length would cause the loop to never advance `pos`, resulting in an infinite loop. The fix adds an additional condition `(len == 0)` to the existing check, so that if a zero-length message is encountered, the driver will warn and break out of the loop, preventing the hang.

### Relationships between modifications

There is only one file modified. The change is localized to a single conditional statement in the USB bulk callback handler. No new functions or data structures were introduced, and no other files were affected. The fix directly addresses the infinite loop vulnerability caused by malformed (zero-length) messages from a broken device.
